title: CDN
subtitle: Anycast edge POPs, tiered origin shielding, stale-while-revalidate caching, and dynamic edge compute.
keyTakeaways: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) terminates TLS/QUIC at hundreds of global Points of Presence (POPs) close to the user, eliminating long-haul TCP handshake RTTs and absorbing 85-99% of read traffic before it reaches the origin.
Origin Shielding funnels cache misses from hundreds of edge POPs through a single regional aggregation POP with request coalescing, preventing thundering-herd origin collapse on cache expiry.
Immutable content-addressed asset URLs (`app.8f92a.js`) paired with `stale-while-revalidate` and surrogate keys provide instant cache invalidation without origin load spikes.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: CDNs do far more than cache static images. By advertising the same IP address from 300+ global locations via BGP Anycast, a CDN terminates the client's TCP and TLS 1.3 / HTTP/3 handshake within 10 milliseconds of the user, then reuses pre-warmed, multiplexed persistent connections over private fiber backbones to your origin.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) terminates TLS/QUIC at hundreds of global Points of Presence (POPs) close to the user, eliminating long-haul TCP handshake RTTs and absorbing 85-99% of read traffic before it reaches the origin.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: Origin Shielding funnels cache misses from hundreds of edge POPs through a single regional aggregation POP with request coalescing, preventing thundering-herd origin collapse on cache expiry.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for CDN:
bullets: **Long TTL + Surrogate-Key Active Purge**: Provides maximizes cache hit ratio (99%+) and shields origin completely until data actually mutates. Best suited for E-commerce product catalogs, CMS/news publishing, and media metadata APIs.

**Short TTL (5-30s) + Stale-While-Revalidate (Micro-Caching)**: Provides zero purge infrastructure needed; automatically bounds staleness to seconds while still absorbing flash spikes. Best suited for Live sports scores, stock tickers, flash-sale inventory counters, and high-fanout social feeds.

Request Coalescing (Collapsed Forwarding): If a popular live-score JSON or video manifest expires at an Edge POP and 5,000 users request it within 20ms, the POP holds 4,999 requests in memory and sends only **1** fetch upstream.

Tiered Caching / Origin Shield: Without shielding, 300 global Edge POPs experiencing a cache miss still send 300 simultaneous requests to the origin. An Origin Shield POP sits right in front of the origin region, collapsing those 300 edge misses into a single origin request.

Content-Addressed Versioning vs Purging: For static bundles (JS/CSS/images), embed the SHA-256 content hash in the filename (`bundle.a1b2c3.js`) with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Never purge static assets: deploy a new HTML pointer.

Tag-Based Instant Invalidation (`Surrogate-Key` / `Cache-Tag`): For dynamic catalog or news pages, tag responses with entity IDs (`article_42`). When an editor updates the article, send a single API call to purge tag `article_42` globally in <150ms.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply CDN across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for E-commerce product catalogs, CMS/news publishing, and media metadata APIs, suited for environments requiring Maximizes cache hit ratio (99%+) and shields origin completely until data actually mutates.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Live sports scores, stock tickers, flash-sale inventory counters, and high-fanout social feeds, where Zero purge infrastructure needed; automatically bounds staleness to seconds while still absorbing flash spikes.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: A CDN's cache hit ratio (CHR) depends on strict Cache Key normalization. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of CDN introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: requires reliable cdc/webhook integration to trigger tag purges; risk of stale data if a purge webhook fails.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: higher steady-state origin traffic for long-tail items with infrequent requests.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for CDN:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Immutable content-addressed asset URLs (`app.8f92a.js`) paired with `stale-while-revalidate` and surrogate keys provide instant cache invalidation without origin load spikes.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Mention **Micro-Caching** (`s-maxage=5, stale-while-revalidate=10` with Request Coalescing) in interviews: even a 5-second CDN cache on a dynamic endpoint reduces a 100,000 RPS flash-crowd spike down to 1 request every 5 seconds at your origin!
